issues.legal_issue: A compromise decree declaring a pre-existing gift ineffective limits the donee’s rights to the widow’s lifetime and leaves the property with the widow as its limited owner.
material_facts: The widow held only a life interest in the property and made a gift before the Hindu Succession Act came into force.
A suit challenged the gift, and the resulting compromise decree declared the gift ineffective as to the land and provided for division after the widow’s death.
The compromise decree allowed the widow to enjoy the property during her lifetime.
issues.conclusion: The compromise decree was to be construed as allowing the widow to enjoy the property during her lifetime while preventing the gift from operating beyond her lifetime; the widow therefore continued as the limited owner of the property.
issues.legal_principle: The terms and effect of the compromise decree must be read as a whole. Here, its declaration that the gift was ineffective, together with its provision for division after the widow’s death, meant that the gift did not divest the widow of her limited interest during her lifetime or bind the reversioners thereafter.

rule.if: property_succession_dispute and widow_had_limited_interest and pre_act_gift_was_declared_ineffective and decree_provided_for_division_after_widows_death

predicates.property_succession_dispute: The dispute concerns succession to property held by a person with a limited interest.
predicates.widow_had_limited_interest: A widow held only a limited interest in the property when the dispute arose.
predicates.pre_act_gift_was_declared_ineffective: A decree declared ineffective a gift the widow had made before the governing succession change.
predicates.decree_provided_for_division_after_widow: The decree provided that the property would be divided after the widow’s death.

issues.definition: When a succession dispute involves a widow’s limited interest, a pre-existing gift declared ineffective, and a decree providing for division after her death, the gift is confined to her lifetime.

issues.legal_issue: A widow whose pre-Act gift was declared ineffective became absolute owner under Section 14 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, and could dispose of the property by a later will.
material_facts: The widow inherited the property from her husband in 1942 with only a life interest.
Although she had made a gift before the Act, the compromise decree declared the gift ineffective, so she remained the limited owner of the property until the Act came into force.
She made a will after the Act came into force, and the lower courts found the will genuine and properly executed.
The High Court nevertheless awarded the respondents possession of half the land that had been the subject of the earlier gift.
issues.conclusion: Section 14 enlarged the widow’s limited estate into an absolute estate because the ineffective gift had not divested her of the property; she therefore had full capacity to make the later will, and the legatees’ claim under it could not be disputed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 converts a female Hindu’s limited estate into an absolute estate where she retains the property. Because the gift here had been declared legally ineffective, the widow remained its owner until the Act applied and could later dispose of it by will. The Court distinguished Lachhman v. Thunia, A.I.R. 1972 H.P. 69, where the property was treated as no longer in the widow’s possession at her death; that reasoning did not apply when the widow remained owner after the purported gift was held ineffective.

rule.if: property_succession_dispute and widow_inherited_property_with_limited_interest and earlier_gift_was_legally_ineffective and widow_retained_property_at_statutory_change and later_will_was_genuine

predicates.property_succession_dispute: The proceeding concerns competing claims to property through succession.
predicates.widow_inherited_property_with_limited_in: A widow inherited property but initially held only a limited interest in it.
predicates.earlier_gift_was_legally_ineffective: A prior gift by the widow was held legally ineffective, leaving her interest in the property intact.
predicates.widow_retained_property_at_statutory_cha: The widow still held the property when the change governing her estate took effect.
predicates.later_will_was_genuine: The widow made a later will that was found genuine and properly executed.

issues.definition: If a widow inherited property with a limited interest, an earlier gift did not divest her, she retained the property when the governing change took effect, and her later will was genuine, she could dispose of the property by will.
